title: Application, Approval and Tier Movement on Personal Credit Cards
content:
**The application.** An application under Personal Credit Cards records the requested tier. The applicant's age in whole years on the application date, taken from the date of birth on the customer profile, must be at least the tier's youngest age to open and, where the tier sets one, no more than its oldest age to open. The applicant's age must meet the tier's age limits on the application date; the age is read from the profile held by Piedmont Crescent Bank before the application is recorded, and is settled by that record rather than by what the applicant states.

**Two tier conditions of entry.** Visa Infinite Private Client requires an active Private Client Checking account, the highest tier of Personal Checking, held by the applicant; the holding is read from the bank's checking records carried under that same customer profile before the application is recorded. Secured Visa requires a security deposit of at least its smallest accepted deposit, and its credit limit always equals the deposit held.

**Who decides.** Approval and decline are underwriting decisions made by the credit system; the agent never decides them.

**What an approval sets.** An approved limit lies between the tier's smallest credit limit assigned and its largest credit limit carried, and the purchase rate between the tier's lowest and highest purchase rates. The cash advance rate is the tier's own. On tiers offering an introductory balance transfer rate, the introductory rate end date is the statement closing date in the cycle, counted from opening, given by the tier's number of introductory cycles.

**Graduation of a secured card.** A secured card is reviewed at the tier's graduation review month after opening and graduates into the tier's graduation destination when the last six statements were all paid on time. Statements are counted backward from the most recent due date before the day of the review, and a statement counts as paid on time when the payments and credits posted from its closing date through its due date totalled at least that statement's minimum payment due; the count stops at the first statement that fails. On graduation the security deposit is returned to a Piedmont Crescent Bank account of the customer or by official check, and the credit limit is kept.

**Other movements between tiers.** Other tier changes at the cardholder's request are allowed between tiers of the same rewards currency only, never into or out of Secured Visa, and keep the limit, the rate and the balance.

*Basis Q&A.* Where an applicant turns the tier's youngest age to open on the application date itself, the age condition is met, the test being at least that age. Where a tier records no oldest age to open, no upper age condition applies to it. Where an applicant asks to move between a tier whose rewards currency is points and one whose rewards currency is cash back, the two currencies differ and the movement is not one this policy allows; where both tiers carry the same currency, and neither is Secured Visa, it is.
